bg-06-01.hint: I don't have money right now.
bg-06-01.why: 돈 ends in a consonant ㄴ, taking the particle 이 before 없어요.

bg-06-01.q: State that you have time today using 시간 and 있어요.
bg-06-01.why: 시간 ends in a consonant, so it takes the subject particle 이: 시간이 있어요.

bg-06-01.hint: Korean does not use 안 with 있어요; the natural negative is 없어요.
bg-06-01.why: The negative counterpart of 있어요 is the separate word 없어요, not 안 있어요.

steps.en: As for me, I have time today.

en: Minsu, do you have time today?
Yes, I have time in the afternoon.
Right now I have no money in my wallet.

bg-06-01.why: Minsu answers '오후에 시간 있어요' (I have time in the afternoon).

bg-06-01.q: Why is the speaker asking for a bank?
options: They have no cash in their wallet
They want to open an account
They are looking for a friend
bg-06-01.why: The speaker explains '지금 지갑에 돈이 없어요' (Right now I have no money in my wallet).

items: Ask and answer whether you have something using 있어요 and 없어요
Use the standalone negative word 없어요 rather than 안 있어요

bg-06-02.hint: I work at the company every day.
bg-06-02.why: 일하다 is an action taking place at a location, so the place takes 에서.

bg-06-02.q: State where you eat using 식당 and 에서.
bg-06-02.why: Studying is an active behavior, so use the dynamic location marker 에서.

bg-06-02.hint: Action verbs like 공부하다 mark their location with 에서 rather than 에.
bg-06-02.why: Use 에서 for locations where an action is performed: 도서관에서 공부해요.

steps.en: I study at home every day.
As for me, I study at home every day.

en: I am at home right now.
I meet a friend at school.
And I study at the library.

bg-06-02.why: The passage starts with '저는 지금 집에 있어요' (I am at home right now).

bg-06-02.q: What does the speaker do at the library tomorrow?
bg-06-02.why: The text says '도서관에서 공부해요' (I study at the library).

items: Distinguish when to use 에 (location/destination) vs 에서 (action location)
Build complete sentences describing where you go and what you do there

bg-06-03.why: Clock times take the time particle 에: 일곱 시에.

bg-06-03.q: Suggest meeting a friend at 3 o'clock using 세 시에 and 만나요.
bg-06-03.why: Specific clock hours take the time particle 에: 세 시에.

bg-06-03.hint: Common relative time words like 내일 do not take 에.
bg-06-03.why: 오늘, 어제, 내일, 지금, and 매일 reject the particle 에: 내일 만나요.

steps.en: I drink coffee in the morning.
As for me, I drink coffee in the morning.

en: I wake up at seven in the morning.
I drink warm coffee in the morning.
And I meet friends on the weekend.
I have an appointment tomorrow at three.

bg-06-03.q: What time does the speaker wake up?
bg-06-03.why: The text says '아침 일곱 시에 일어나요' (I wake up at seven in the morning).
The text says '내일 세 시에 약속이 있어요' (I have an appointment tomorrow at three).

items: Attach 에 to specific clock times and parts of the day
Remember which time words (like 내일, 오늘) drop the particle

bg-06-04.hint: There is a wallet in the bag.
bg-06-04.why: 지갑 ends in a consonant ㅂ, so it takes the subject particle 이 before 있어요.

bg-06-04.q: State what is in your bag or room using 에 and 이/가 있어요.
bg-06-04.why: Location takes 에 and 우산 ends in a consonant ㄴ, taking the particle 이.

bg-06-04.hint: 열쇠 ends in the vowel ㅚ, so it takes 가.
bg-06-04.why: Nouns ending in a vowel take the subject particle 가: 열쇠 + 가 → 열쇠가 있어요.

steps.en: There is an umbrella at home.
Right now there is an umbrella at home.

en: However, I do not have an umbrella in my bag.
There is a big umbrella at home.
I take the subway and go home.

bg-06-04.q: What is the problem the speaker faces?
options: They have no umbrella in their bag
bg-06-04.why: The passage notes '가방에 우산이 없어요' (I do not have an umbrella in my bag).

bg-06-04.q: How is the speaker going home?
bg-06-04.why: The text says '지하철을 타고 집에 가요' (I take the subway and go home).

items: Specify where an object exists using location-에 item-이/가 있어요
Pick between 이 and 가 accurately based on the final consonant
